A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DisCL research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including rendered equations, figures, and tables, support reliable comparison despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments, ablations, and synthetic-image analyses on ImageNet-LT, CIFAR100-LT, iNaturalist2018, and iWildCam.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds ResNet-34 evaluations, synthetic-data scaling experiments, and worst-class performance analysis.

M1.justification: Both versions retain image-guided diffusion, CLIPScore filtering, the Diverse-to-Specific curriculum, and adaptive guidance selection using learning progress. Algorithms 1–2 receive clearer indexing and notation without changing their procedures.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same four datasets and the same long-tail and low-quality classification tasks, including iWildCam ID/OOD evaluation. Additional backbone, data-volume, and worst-class analyses remain within this coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 4 adds FLYP + ALIA to the reported iWildCam comparison. v1 names ALIA in its baseline discussion but provides no corresponding result in Table 5. The other main comparison methods are retained.

E3.justification: v3 extends evaluation to ResNet-34 on ImageNet-LT and CIFAR100-LT, varies synthetic-tail-data amounts from 1× to 5× against a no-synthetic baseline, and evaluates worst-k classes for five k values. Existing benchmark splits, primary metrics, and documented training schedules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 5.4/Figure 5 tests whether increasing synthetic-data volume continues helping tail classes or harms other classes. New Appendix A.8/Table 10 examines whether DisCL particularly benefits Balanced Softmax's worst-performing classes. These substantially extend the analysis beyond the retained guidance, curriculum, filtering-threshold, and failure-case studies.

E5.justification: Both report three runs for long-tail experiments and three random seeds for iWildCam, retain the same parenthesized uncertainty values in corresponding iWildCam rows, and identify ablation error bars as standard deviations. No new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: In Table 2 at CIFAR100-LT imbalance ratio 100, CE + CUDA overall accuracy changes from 29.02 to 29.85, while CE + DisCL few/overall accuracy changes from 13.65/39.91 to 10.65/30.91; the PDFs do not explain whether these are corrections or reruns. v3 also adds FLYP + ALIA OOD/ID F1 scores of 36.9/52.6, ResNet-34 results in Tables 7–8, scaling results, and worst-k improvements of 4.5–7.6 percentage points in Table 10. The principal ImageNet-LT and iWildCam DisCL table results are retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 retain the same diffusion, guidance, and learning-progress approximation relations. Revised sample/guidance indexing and explicit guidance dependence in Algorithm 2 clarify existing mathematics; no new theorem, proof, or substantive formal assumption appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a synthetic-to-real data spectrum and two curricula improve learning from scarce or low-quality images. The headline ImageNet-LT and iWildCam gains are unchanged; the additional experiments support existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the scaling results as supporting a 3× synthetic-data choice and diminishing returns beyond roughly 3–4×. Appendix A.3 newly attributes some head-class degradation to combining class reweighting with excessive tail-class signals, while A.8 emphasizes complementarity with Balanced Softmax on difficult classes. Existing generation, filtering, and prompt-related limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 5.4 newly specifies a 3× synthetic-tail-data training budget, and Appendix A.3 states that ResNet-34 uses the existing experimental settings. This adds documentation without establishing a change to earlier experiments. The detailed hyperparameter tables, hardware information, and actual code-link destinations are retained.

R1.justification: v3 explicitly credits Meng et al.'s SDEdit for the initialization-step approach and adds discussion of feedback-guided synthesis, DiffuLT, DataDream, and minority guidance. It removes the Azizi and DatasetDM references and sharpens the contrast with large-scale or specially trained generators. The overall positioning around image-guided generative curricula remains.

P1.justification: v3 revises the title, condenses the separate Applications section into Methodology Section 3.2, rewrites portions of related work and application explanations, and clarifies algorithm notation. Most introductory, experimental, analytical, and concluding prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column layout, extensively relocates tables and appendix illustrations, rearranges the ablation panels, and replaces v1's large-CLIP numerical Table 4 with Figure 3 bar charts. It also adds the scaling figure and ResNet-34/worst-class tables, revises the overview diagram, and removes the buffalo example from Figure 2.

improvement.justification: The added ALIA comparison, ResNet-34 checks, and data-volume/worst-class analyses make the empirical support more complete, while SDEdit attribution clarifies provenance. These are useful incremental gains. Reporting remains imperfect: the retained 2.6-point nearest-baseline claim does not match v3 Table 4, and the replacement large-CLIP chart labels the model L/16 while the accompanying text specifies L/14.
